labels: Confirmed: Blizzard or the game files say it directly. Likely: strong evidence, not Blizzard's own words. Speculative: a guess the page marks as one.

pages.title: Druid
pages.blurb: A druid can fill any role in a party: Balance casts damage spells, Feral shapeshifts into Cat for melee damage or Bear to tank, and Restoration heals over time, at the cost of the extra utility other classes bring, such as interrupts…

pages.title: Hunter
pages.blurb: A hunter is a ranged damage dealer with a pet: damage is its only combat role, though the pet can tank in solo and small-group play, and it has the longest range of any class but a dead zone within 8 yards of an enemy.

pages.title: Mage spellbook
pages.blurb: Every mage spell with its ranks, levels and top-rank values, from client build 70450 (Oct 16) as read by wowforevertools on Oct 18.

pages.title: Mage talents
pages.blurb: The three mage trees row by row. The frame (first point at 10, medals at 11, 16, 21 and 31 points, dual spec at 40) is Blizzard's Oct 7 deep dive; the row layout, rank counts and per-rank values are one datamine site's read of client…

pages.title: Mage
pages.blurb: A mage is a ranged damage dealer in cloth with strong area damage and Polymorph crowd control: Arcane, Fire and Frost differ in how they deal damage, and the mage is fragile and dies fast in melee.

pages.title: Classes overview
pages.blurb: World of Warcraft: Forever has nine classes: Druid, Hunter, Mage, Paladin, Priest, Rogue, Shaman, Warlock and Warrior. The roles below come from Blizzard's class deep dives.

pages.title: Paladin
pages.blurb: A paladin is a hybrid that can tank, heal or deal damage: Protection tanks, Holy is the strongest single-target healer, and Retribution is a competitive melee damage dealer, all built on Seals and Judgement, with no interrupt and no…

pages.title: Priest
pages.blurb: A priest is a healer first: it heals with both direct heals and heals over time, shields allies with damage absorbs, and in the Shadow tree switches to damage over time, though it wears cloth and has few ways to escape, so it leans on…

pages.title: Rogue
pages.blurb: A rogue is a stealthy melee damage dealer: it opens fights from Stealth, uses poisons, daggers and other weapons, and adds crowd control such as Sap and Distract that a party can use when there are too many enemies to tank.

pages.title: Shaman
pages.blurb: A shaman is a totem user who buffs, heals and solves problems for a party: it can be a melee or spell damage dealer or a healer, with Enhancement able to tank for a short while in small groups, and it wears mail and a shield but has no…

pages.title: Tanking
pages.blurb: Blizzard's deep dives build three full tanks with a taunt each: Protection Warrior and Feral Druid (Sep 30) and Protection Paladin (Oct 15).

pages.title: Warlock
pages.blurb: A warlock is a ranged damage dealer in cloth who fights alongside a demon pet: Affliction uses damage over time and drains, Demonology empowers the pet and the warlock, Destruction burns with direct fire, and the warlock is physically…

pages.title: Warrior
pages.blurb: A warrior is a melee fighter that can tank or deal damage: Protection holds enemies, Arms and Fury hit hard, and it builds Rage from fighting, though it has few ways to recover from heavy damage.

pages.title: City of Dalaran
pages.blurb: A new 28 to 33 dungeon under Dalaran, which now sits in Alterac Mountains. It opened for beta testing on Oct 8. One party member needs the Dalaran Sewer Key, a Heart of Disruption reward on both factions.

pages.title: Excavation Site Wetlands
pages.blurb: A new dungeon through Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands, added to the beta on Oct 1. Blizzard's own band moved: Kaivax listed 24 to 29 on Sep 14, the Oct 1 notes say 26 to 31, and Method's page says 26 to 33; quests open at 24 and…

pages.title: Hall of Thanes
pages.blurb: A new 13 to 18 dungeon under Ironforge's High Seat, open from the first day of the beta. Four bosses; Durgen Dirgehammer's 8 second AoE fear and Faldrim Anvilmar's dispellable curse are the mechanics guide sites call out.

pages.title: New dungeons 35 to 60
pages.blurb: Five of the nine new dungeons sit above the beta's level 30 cap, so none has been played outside Blizzard. Kaivax's Sep 14 list gives the bands and corrected Krol'dok Stronghold from an earlier 40 to 55 listing to 40 to 45.

pages.title: Dungeons overview
pages.blurb: Forever has no automatic dungeon finder. The Group Finder is a listing board with four tabs; groups list themselves and invite by hand, and nothing teleports a party to the door.

pages.title: Returning dungeons 13 to 22
pages.blurb: The Classic dungeons that run from the first Group Finder entry level to the low twenties, with the beta Group Finder entry level (GF) from an Oct 6 client read and the Forever-specific facts the guides recorded.

pages.title: Returning dungeons 23 to 30
pages.blurb: The Classic dungeons at the top of the beta's level range: the Stockade, Razorfen Kraul, Gnomeregan and the four Scarlet Monastery wings, with the beta Group Finder entry level (GF) from an Oct 6 client read.

pages.title: Returning dungeons 30 plus
pages.blurb: Razorfen Downs and Uldaman opened in beta on Oct 1 at 25+ and 30+; everything from Zul'Farrak up never ran in beta, so quest names are Forever data from Wowhead's table and rewards and loot are Classic until proven otherwise.

pages.title: Ruins of Lordaeron
pages.blurb: A new 15 to 20 dungeon outside the Undercity front gate, open from the beta's first day. Six bosses including two optional ones, all undead, with a 30 minute Ghoul Plague disease on trash. Six Horde quests and four Alliance.

pages.title: Beta and stress test
pages.blurb: The closed beta ran from September 17, 2026 at level cap 20 and then 30, the free stress test on launch hardware ran on October 21 at 2:00 PM PDT (wiped afterward), and Blizzard closed the beta on October 23.

pages.title: Launch
pages.blurb: World of Warcraft: Forever launches Wed, Nov 4, 2026, 6 PM ET (3 PM PT), the same moment worldwide, with no early access.

pages.title: Pre-purchase dates
pages.blurb: The pre-purchase post sets the calendar around launch: Invite-A-Friend codes by email from October 20, Early Name Reservation October 27 to November 3 (PST) for accounts with a pack, friend access November 4 to 11, and the Collection…

pages.title: Raids open Dec 9
pages.blurb: Blizzard's raid preview opens all three raids on December 9, 2026: Barrow Deeps (10 players, 8 bosses), Hyjal Summit (20 players, 13 bosses) and Onyxia's Lair (40 players). Every raid is planned to reset each week.

pages.title: The beta in four builds
pages.blurb: Read as a story: Sep 24 was a polish pass, Oct 1 opened ten levels and tightened XP and the economy, Oct 8 undid early detours from Classic math, and Oct 15 was the largest block, touching every race and making core buffs raid-wide.

pages.title: Stress test Oct 21
pages.blurb: Blizzard's Server Slam on launch hardware ran Wednesday Oct 21, 2026; its date, start time, access, install path, wipe and the move from Oct 19 are on the Beta and stress test page.

pages.title: Gear ladder 10 to 35
pages.blurb: What exists for casters, healers and tanks between 10 and 35: the mage quest chain, the wand ladder, crafted mail and leather, and the stat orders guides argue over.

pages.title: XP and leveling rules
pages.blurb: The XP curve is Classic's, 4,084,700 to 60 with no global buff; Blizzard changed the world instead, with 1,000+ new quests. Rested XP works as in Classic and cooked food adds a small bonus.

pages.title: Leveling zones
pages.blurb: Four zones are new (Zephras Isle, Riverglades, Shen'dralas, Mount Hyjal) and two were reworked (Wetlands, Desolace).

pages.title: Alchemy
pages.blurb: Healing Potions moved to First Aid; Alchemy keeps mana potions and gains a low-level Minor Arcane Elixir. The Favor vendor sells Mender's Potions and three stat elixirs with no caster elixir in the visible text.

pages.title: Comprehension and Study (mage)
pages.blurb: Comprehension is a mage-only minor tradeskill trained at level 6 with a Comprehend Scroll spell. Untranslated scrolls drop at random from mobs; deciphering raises skill while the scroll is not grey, with tiers at skill 1, 15, 50 and…

pages.title: Enchanting
pages.blurb: Apprentice Enchanting has no level requirement, Disenchant lives in the Professions window, and new low recipes make 1 to 70 cheaper than Classic.

pages.title: Engineering
pages.blurb: Bomb satchels fill the thrown slot with no ammo and deal area damage; SAF-T versions let non-engineers throw them. Four satchel recipes sit on the Favor vendor with rising skill and price gates.

pages.title: Professions overview
pages.blurb: Blizzard counts over 600 new recipes and ties crafting to camping and the trade companies. Training tiers follow character level (Apprentice 5, Journeyman 10, Expert 20, Artisan 35) with caps of 75, 150, 225 and 300, and most recipes…

pages.title: Tailoring
pages.blurb: Tailoring has the deepest Favor vendor: six-piece school sets at level 12 for 30 Favor a piece, with Friendly and Honored upgrade lines for levels 35 to 50; every Favor piece binds on pickup.

pages.title: Darkspear Islands
pages.blurb: The new battleground: 15 against 15, levels 30 to 60, off Dustwallow Marsh. Four capture points plus a central flag scored at a held base; first team to 2,000 wins.

pages.title: PvP progression
pages.blurb: Blizzard's Oct 7 post sets up two currencies: Honor, which is spent on a blue set and an epic set, and Rank Points, which are never spent and accrue from battlegrounds and PvP quests under a weekly cap. Fourteen ranks each pay a reward.

pages.title: Alliance racials
pages.blurb: Human, Dwarf, Gnome and Night Elf racials as Blizzard's Create the Hero article lists them, with the Oct 15 dev-notes changes layered on top.

pages.title: Horde racials
pages.blurb: Orc, Troll, Undead and Tauren racials from Blizzard's Create the Hero article with the Oct 15 and Oct 26 changes applied.

pages.title: Races and class combinations
pages.blurb: Forever keeps the nine original classes and eight original races, adds the Skyborne on both factions, and opens six combinations Classic never allowed: Orc Mage, Troll Warlock, Undead Paladin, Human Hunter, Gnome Priest and Dwarf Shaman.

pages.title: Skyborne
pages.blurb: One race, two cultures: the High Order join the Alliance and the Windshapers the Horde, with the faction picked at creation.

pages.title: Barrow Deeps
pages.blurb: The 10-player raid in Mount Hyjal. Everything specific to the inside is datamine: eight boss names in no confirmed order, a Brooch of the Wardens that opens a Vord'anaar Prison area, and Corrupted shards named after each boss.

pages.title: Hyjal Summit
pages.blurb: The 20-player raid in Mount Hyjal, a brand new zone. Four partial boss names come from one commercial datamine. No attunement per the devs on podcast episode 3.

pages.title: Level 60 gear and buffs
pages.blurb: Blizzard confirms new tier sets; every bonus below is third-party datamine, never seen on a live tooltip. Ion Hazzikostas told Windows Central that Classic-style world-buff farming is removed from raiding; how is unpublished.

pages.title: Onyxia's Lair
pages.blurb: Onyxia is a black dragon fought in a 40-player raid; it opens Dec 9 with Barrow Deeps and Hyjal Summit.

pages.title: Library books and secrets
pages.blurb: Forty hidden library books (26 in Eastern Kingdoms, 14 in Kalimdor) turn in to librarians in Stormwind and Undercity for rewards at 10, 20 and 25 books; the hunt is open to every class.

pages.title: Camping objects
pages.blurb: The object list per profession is Warcraft Tavern's beta read of the client, not Blizzard text: each tier 1 object copies a class buff, costs a few starter materials, and has tier 2 and 3 upgrades at skill 140 and 300.

pages.title: Camping
pages.blurb: Blizzard's Sep 13 deep dive turns the Cooking Fire into a Basic Campfire with vendors, repairs, crafting workspaces and 1-hour buffs.

pages.title: Earning gold
pages.blurb: Gold comes from a few usual ways in Classic-era WoW: quest rewards, selling loot to vendors, selling gathered materials, the Auction House and professions.

pages.title: Factions
pages.blurb: On Normal, RP and Hardcore an account can hold both factions; on PvP Blizzard allows one faction per account per region, set by the first character created there.

pages.title: Gold, riding and economy rules
pages.blurb: Riding is Burning Crusade-style: the cost sits in the training and a mount comes with it; there is no flying.

pages.title: Layers
pages.blurb: Layers are invisible copies of the world inside one ruleset. Testers described invites pulling players onto the inviter's layer, world PvP fights ending when someone was moved, an early Layer Now button that did nothing, and no sign of…

pages.title: Legacy perks
pages.blurb: All 21 perks across the Adventure, Resourcefulness and Professions trees, from beta build 70425 client data cross-checked with Warcraft Tavern and Method; one point per rank, values per rank unless stated.

pages.title: Legacy system
pages.blurb: Legacy is an account-wide track of 65 challenges worth one point each, shared by every non-Hardcore character across rulesets.

pages.title: Merchant's Favor
pages.blurb: Two trade companies, one per faction, run the Waylaid Supplies loop: crates drop in the world or sell on the auction house, each wants a bundle of materials, and turning one in pays Favor.

pages.title: Character names
pages.blurb: Every character has two names; the full pair must be unique within the region, so either part can repeat and a group can share a surname. The second name can be hidden on nameplates but still shows in chat.

pages.title: Packs and pricing
pages.blurb: Forever has no box price: access comes with a World of Warcraft subscription or Game Time. Three optional packs add the Skyborne race, name reservation, cosmetics and friend codes; none lists early access.

pages.title: Reputations
pages.blurb: Fourteen new factions appear in the beta client according to one commercial site (Sep 22); a Kami Labs leak counted 17, so the total may move. Only the Darkspear Islands pair has Blizzard text.

pages.title: Rulesets
pages.blurb: There is no realm list: the choice that used to be a server is a ruleset. Normal, PvP, RP and, since Blizzard's Oct 22 update, RP-PvP exist at launch; Hardcore follows later.

pages.title: Client and addons
pages.blurb: Forever is not the 2019 Classic client. Blizzard's Sept 15 developer update, quoted on the wiki, says it shares Mainline's UI architecture and the vast majority of 12.1.5 APIs; the beta reports interface 16001 and only a Forever-tagged…

pages.title: Macros and settings
pages.blurb: Because the UI is the modern Mainline one, the macro system is expected to match it: mouseover, focus and cursor targets, modifier conditions, /stopcasting, /cancelaura and /castsequence.
